newsitem.title: UK: 1996 global advertising spending seen up 7.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: 1996 global advertising spending seen up 7.7 pct.

text.p: Worldwide advertising spending for 1996 is expected to be 7.7 percent ahead of 1995 in current prices, and 4.1 percent ahead on inflation-adjusted prices, Zenith Media said on Monday.

Zenith, the media buying and planning arm of advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc, said it sees global adspend reaching $282.3 billion in 1996 in current prices, up from $262.2 billion in 1995.
"We continue to forecast 1996 to be the high point of real growth to 1999, with outlook of steady real growth in benign world economic conditions," Zenith said.

"Despite their problems, the developing regions of Asia and to a lesser degree Latin America remain the best prospects for long-term advertising growth at roughly double the rates the West can achieve," Zenith said.
The developing regions of Asia and Latin America are expected to account for 20 percent of global adspend in 1999, up from 18 percent currently, Zenith said.
